Definition: from G5259 and G756; to begin under (quietly), i.e. come into existence (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as an auxiliary to a principal (verb):--after, behave, live.
BiblicalUsage: hypárchō is how Scripture says to be, to exist, to have. In Matthew 19:21, the text says "and thou shalt have treasure in heaven." In Luke 7:25, the text says "and live delicately."
TheologicalSignificance: I take hypárchō to mean that life is God's gift, and it is meant to be lived with Him, not apart from Him. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
